title: Sorcery and Divination
lead: The Bible forbids spells, divination and consulting the dead (Exodus 22:18; Deuteronomy 18:10–12), from the Egyptian magicians and the medium at Endor to Simon Magus and the books burned at Ephesus. The early modern witch trials quoted these laws.

sections.b: Pharaoh's magicians copy Moses' first signs (Exodus 7:11, 22). The Covenant Code says a sorceress must not be left alive (Exodus 22:18), and Deuteronomy 18:10–12 lists the forbidden arts: divination, omens, spells, mediums and calling up the dead, setting against them the prophet God will raise up (Deuteronomy 18:15). Saul expels mediums but then consults one at Endor (1 Samuel 28). In the New Testament Simon the magician is rebuked (Acts 8:9–24), new believers at Ephesus burn their books of magic (Acts 19:19), and Paul lists sorcery among the works of the flesh (Galatians 5:20; Revelation 21:8).
